subject: Task 21.8 — corrected release build, full suite, reproducible artifact, and release documentation
summary: Independent re-verification of every checkable claim in the task 21.8 worker report. A fourth clean build from my own git export (1,102 tracked files, /tmp/final-review/test-quality/repro-c, a path the worker did not use) reproduced the recorded archive identity exactly: 619,636 bytes, SHA-256 3e59cb06dfd09da4df71e4e4a1c608b664db61326b0184c63cf846fcc502d277, MD5 f3b50a91c7cb63d9560316d8abe2f9dc, 7 entries, all stamped 2000-01-01 00:00, and byte-identical (cmp) to the repository archive and to the worker's export A. The 7 per-entry SHA-256 values in the release doc match my extraction exactly. All four documented suite tiers reproduce exactly: default with the archive present 0/1,937/66/2,003; default without the archive 0/1,934/69/2,003; host-guarded against the verified pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 host (/tmp/arrtags-14.3/jellyfin, Jellyfin.Api.dll present, console.log records 'Jellyfin version: 12.0.0') 0/1,957/46/2,003; forced-native with the recorded probe sysroot 0/2,024/21/2,045. The skip taxonomy is exactly as documented and matches the source attribute counts (20 JellyfinHostFact + 41 SkiaNativeFact + 4 SkiaNativeTheory + 1 NonCanonicalRuntimeFact = 66; +3 PackagedPluginFact when no archive is present; host-guarded 46 = 45 native + 1; forced-native 21 = 20 host + 1). The +10 delta over task 21.3's 1,993 is independently confirmed: the focused filter FullyQualifiedName~ProviderRedirectTransportTests gives 0/10/0/10. The corrected-artifact claim is confirmed: the preserved superseded archive /tmp/21.8/superseded-21.3.zip re-hashes to 505804992a50d7aa073b07cfaa8dc0c8ac9a95041a7c394d8bd54dd959f90762 / 619,538 bytes / MD5 3100aae94a2b4aedf222eca040675271, and a per-entry comparison shows only ArrTags.dll changed (1,346,560 / 8d7b25c6… -> 1,347,072 / eae2cbab…); the other six entries are byte-identical. The change set is documentation and manifest only (PLANS.md, docs/plan/state.json, docs/release/build-and-release.md, manifest.json, 4 files, 90 insertions / 47 deletions), so no guard was weakened, no skip was added or widened, and no determinism or isolation property of the suite changed. Guard honesty is good: the release doc states in 'Known environment notes' that no automated test guards byte-identity and that a pack-release.cs or build-property regression would not fail the suite; the P1 limitation and the manifest checksum equality are stated as procedure, not as test coverage; and the release checklist items are intentionally unchecked. I also cross-checked the doc's 1.1.0.0 per-entry comparison against the preserved 1.1.0.0 archive and it is accurate (ArrTags.dll, ArrTags.deps.json, build.yaml differ; the three licenses/ entries and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md unchanged). No BLOCKER or HIGH finding. One open MEDIUM documentation-honesty gap: docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md still names the superseded 21.3 candidate (619,538 bytes / 5058…) as 'the v1.2 release candidate' without a superseded marker, which the worker disclosed in its known_limitations and which task 21.9 (owner of the corrected live matrix) should close.

findings.description: docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md section 'v1.2 live matrix (Phase 21 task 21.4)' still presents the superseded task 21.3 archive (619,538 bytes, SHA-256 505804992a50d7aa073b07cfaa8dc0c8ac9a95041a7c394d8bd54dd959f90762) as 'the v1.2 release candidate' with no superseded marker, while the canonical release doc marks that same hash superseded and records the corrected 3e59cb06… identity. A reader following the testing host document to install or re-run the v1.2 candidate would install the pre-SEC-21.5-01 build, whose provider clients re-send X-Api-Key to a 3xx Location origin. The statement is historically accurate as a record of what task 21.4 ran, so it is not a false claim about the past; it is a stale pointer to a superseded artifact from the current-state documentation tree. The 21.8 worker disclosed this in its known_limitations as outside its delegated surface.

findings.description: No automated test establishes that the packaged ArrTags.dll (1,347,072 bytes, SHA-256 eae2cbab…) is the same code the 10 ProviderRedirectTransportTests exercised. The equivalence rests on a chain of recorded facts — the reproducible build, the recorded per-entry hash, and the fact that the packaged entry is the compiler output of the same source — not on a test assertion. This is disclosed and pre-existing (limitation P1, and the 'Known environment notes' bullet in the release doc), and it is not introduced or worsened by task 21.8, which changed no code. It is recorded here so that the corrected-dll claim is not read as a test-guaranteed property.

findings.description: The reproducibility evidence is sound for what it claims and the documentation does not overstate it. I added a fourth clean-build run from an export the worker did not use, and additionally re-packaged in that export after a full test run, reproducing the identical SHA-256 and MD5 both times — so the artifact is not perturbed by the suite. The release doc states three runs, which is true; my run is additional corroboration, not a discrepancy. The doc explicitly says byte-identity is not test-guarded, is demonstrated only with the pinned SDK, and the release checklist that would consume the identity is left unchecked. The golden path cannot auto-approve: RenderGoldenTests has no writer, auto-update, or auto-approval path and compares decoded pixels, encoded bytes, output hash, and output fingerprint.

limitations: My checks cover the recorded artifact identity, the four documented suite tiers, the corrected-dll delta, the documentation's counts and guard statements, and the determinism/isolation posture. I did not audit the SEC-21.5-01 transport fix's behavioural coverage itself; that was task 21.7's test-quality review and is task 21.10's release-security-review scope.
I did not run a live Jellyfin instance. The host-guarded tier reflects over the pinned 12.0.0 assemblies only, and the live pinned-host matrix for the corrected artifact is task 21.9.

The forced-native tier's counts depend on the recorded probe sysroot at /tmp/arrtags-skia-probe, which is outside the repository and is not itself version-controlled or re-creatable from the tree; I verified the tier reproduces with that sysroot as documented, not that the sysroot is reproducible.

Byte-reproducibility is demonstrated only with the pinned SDK (global.json 10.0.0 latestMinor, validated with 10.0.401). A different SDK could change compiler or deflate output; limitation P1 records this and task 21.8 does not change it.

artifacts/ArrTags_1.2.0.0.zip is gitignored build output, not a committed tree member. The committed manifest.json checksum refers to the locally produced corrected artifact, so the identity is not verifiable from a fresh clone without rebuilding.

scripts/check-docs.sh currently exits non-zero solely on the contract-defined interim state for section 9 (task 21.8 has a worker report but no reviewer report yet). Every other section, including the artifact-identity agreement, is ok. This clears when the orchestrator adds and registers the implementation-reviewer report; it is not a test-quality defect.
